 P.A. TO JUDGE sou.
 ASHOK BHUSHAN, Ag.CJ & A.M.SHAFFIQUE, J.
J U D G M E N T Ashok Bhushan, Ag.CJ Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader.
No notice need to be issued to private respondents 4 to 10 in view of the order which is being passed.

2. By this writ petition, the petitioner has prayed for a mandamus commanding the third respondent to provide adequate and effective police protection to conduct business in Hotel Devasura Inn,
Chavakkad, against the threat imposed by respondents 4 to 10.
3. The petitioner's case is that an incident took place on 18.8.2014 in which the private respondents entered into the hotel and caused damages and physical injury also.
Crime No.965 of 2014 has already been registered.

Bimal M.B. Manager vs The Director General Of Police on 23 May, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162343601/

sentences.text: 4. Learned Government Pleader submits that no further complaints have been received.
He further submits that in the event any request is received from the petitioner, the police shall ensure that there is no law and order problem in the area and appropriate measures shall be taken.
5. Considering the fact that crime has already been registered and police is making investigation we are of the view that no purpose will be served in keeping the writ petition pending.
We observe that in the event any complaint is submitted by the petitioner pointing out any obstruction, the third respondent shall take appropriate measures to maintain law and order.
The writ petition is disposed of.

Sd/-
ASHOK BHUSHAN, ACTING CHIEF JUSTICE Sd/-
A.M.SHAFFIQUE, JUDGE.
